key_insight: Rectified-flow generation coupled with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent optimization of printable bone-scaffold microstructures and their spatial arrangement.
engineering_relevance: The framework designs highly porous implants that closely match target bone mechanics under multiple loads, with potential applications in metal additive manufacturing.
method: Generate periodic lattice microstructures using a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine latent designs using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize unit-cell geometry and spatial assignment under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: All eight rabbit-benchmark refinements achieved under 1% error across six target moduli; human femoral designs reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance within 2% and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational benchmarks but does not establish fabricated-scaffold performance or biological integration.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
